O: The chart displays a single orange line connecting four data points.
The x-axis is labeled 'Year' with tick marks for 2017, 2018, 2019, and 2020.
The y-axis is labeled 'Referral volume (thousands)' with a scale from 100 to 150.
The data points are located at approximately (2017, 102), (2018, 118), (2019, 134), and (2020, 150).
The line exhibits a consistent upward slope from left to right across the entire visible x-axis range.
records.B: Assuming the visible 2017-2020 data points represent the relevant trend for the 'full 2013-2020 utilization pattern' requested in the goal, the visual evidence of a steady increase across all displayed years supports the reading of 'sustained period-wide growth'.

O: The chart's x-axis begins at the year 2017.
The y-axis values increase from just above 100 at the start to 150 at the end.
There are no data points or line segments visible for the years 2013, 2014, 2015, or 2016.
The slope of the line segment connecting 2019 to 2020 appears visually similar to the slope of the segment connecting 2017 to 2018.
records.B: Assuming the 'full 2013-2020 utilization pattern' strictly requires data from 2013, the visible chart only provides evidence for the 2017-2020 window. A reading of 'recent upward shift' might be inferred if the user assumes the growth is a new phenomenon limited to this visible window, though the visible data itself shows growth across all four plotted years.
